spans.s:
Nīlaṅgu is the name of a species of ‘worm’ in the yajurveda Saṃhitās in the list of victims at the aśvamedha, or ‘horse sacrifice.’
Foot notes taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 5, 11, 1; Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 14, 11 (v.l. nīlāṅgu); Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxiv. 30. Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 98.

Nīla-śīrṣṇī, ‘black-headed,’ is the name of an unknown animal in the list of victims at the aśvamedha, or ‘horse sacrifice,’ in the taittirīya Saṃhitā.
Foot notes v. 5, 15, 1. Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 99.

Nīlāgalasāla, or, as the Paippalāda version reads, Nīlākalasālā, is the name, according to the commentator, of a graincreeper in the Atharvaveda.
Foot notes vi. 16, 4. Cf. Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 292, 293; Bloomfield, Hymns of the Atharvaveda, 466.
